Ufm1 inhibits apoptosis in response to endoplasmatic reticulum stress.
UFM1 is a new member ubiquitin-like protein that is induced by ER stress and that it protects macrophages from apoptosis by suppressing ER stress response.

ubiquitin-fold modifier  1 (Ufm 1 ) is upregulated in resident peritoneal mouse macrophages and the mouse macrophagic cell line Raw264.7 under ER stress conditions, and Ufm1 protects the macrophages against ER stress-induced  apoptosis.

the function of Ufm1 in the ER stress response and apoptosis in Raw264. 7 cells.
the function of Ufm1 in macrophages,
the role of Ufm1 in the ER stress response and the apoptosis of Raw 264.7 cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ufm1 is a novel gene that is upregulated in response to ER stresses and that protects macrophages from apoptosis.

Ufm1 inhibits apoptosis in macrophage cells through the regulation of the ER stress pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ubiquitin-fold modifier Ⅰ (Ufm1), which is a member of the ubiquitine-like protein family, is upregulated in resident peritoneal mouse macrophages (diabetic mice) and Raw264.7 mouse macrophages treated with endoplasmic stress-inducers, thapsigargine and tunicamycin.
Ufm1 inhibits ER stress-induced apoptosis of macrophages by suppressing ER stress response.
Ufm1 may play a role in protecting macrophages from apoptosis induced by ER stress.
The main takeaway from our work is that
UFM1 is a novel gene protecting against ER stress-induced macrophage apoptosis.
Ufm1 inhibits apoptosis through the suppression of the ER stress pathway.
Ufm1 inhibits ER stress-induced apoptosis by suppressing the ER stress response.
